h: Canals, Outlets and a Rainy-Day Plan B
p: Blue Planet's spot in Ellesmere Port makes it one of the easiest attractions in the North West to build a day around. It sits right by junction 10 of the M53, so it's handy from Chester, Liverpool, North Wales and the Wirral, and there's no fiddling about with city centre parking.

Once you've finished under the waves, Cheshire Oaks Designer Outlet is practically next door, with a huge spread of shops and places to eat. It's a classic split: one half of the family goes shopping, the other half has another lap of the shark tunnel. A few minutes away, the National Waterways Museum sits at the old docks where the Shropshire Union Canal meets the Manchester Ship Canal. It's full of historic narrowboats, old warehouses and stories about the people who lived and worked on the canals, and it's a nice contrast to the modern aquarium.

Aquariums are at their best when you take them slowly. Rather than racing to the tunnel, let younger children stop at the smaller tanks; spotting a camouflaged fish or a hidden eel is half the fun. Try going later in the afternoon on a dry day, as wet weekends and school holidays bring in the crowds.

Back in Chester, the River Dee is lovely for an evening wander, with boat trips running from the riverside in the warmer months and the old suspension bridge over to the meadows. It's the perfect gentle finish after an indoor day.
